newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin gives Lebed go-ahead for NATO visit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin gives Lebed go-ahead for NATO visit.

text.p: Alexander Lebed, the blunt former Soviet paratroop general who now is Boris Yeltsin's security adviser, will visit the headquarters of one-time arch-enemy NATO next month, the Russian president's spokesman said on Friday.

Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, confirmed at a news briefing that the president had approved the trip in response to an invitation to the western defence alliance's Brussels base extended by NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.
The visit, from October 6 to 9, will be the first ever to the West for Lebed, who makes no secret of his ambition to be Russia's next president.
Lebed, 46, has already gained a reputation in the West for sabre-rattling but has also drawn praise for his efforts to end a bloody, 21-month conflict in the breakaway region of Chechnya.

In a newspaper interview this week, Lebed said he would take a "tough line" during the Brussels trip. Repeating his criticism of U.S. raids on Iraq, he said that if Russia were ever a target, "I would hit back instantly. With everything we've got."

Lebed, who spent most of his 20-odd year army career preparing for a global confrontation with NATO, became Yeltsin's national security adviser last June after coming third in the first round of the presidential election.
He has made a series of controversial statements about the West and NATO's plans to incorporate countries of eastern and central Europe.
Britain's Daily Telegraph newspaper this week quoted him as saying Moscow would hit back at German and U.S. industrial interests if the West allowed NATO expansion.
He said in the interview that he would explain his opposition to NATO expansion in the visit.

Moscow opposes the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's planned expansion. It says it would threaten Russia's security and has threatened to take unspecified measures if the Western alliance goes ahead with its plans.
Defence Minister Igor Rodionov set out Moscow's opposition to NATO expansion on Thursday at talks with U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry in Norway.
Perry said on Friday he would meet Rodionov twice more this year in efforts to convince Russia expansion poses no threat.

Russian news agencies reported that Rodionov would meet Yeltsin in hospital on Saturday for talks on the problems facing the country's hard-up armed forces and the options for military reform. Lebed, in typically outspoken remarks this week, said the army was on the verge of mutiny over unpaid wages.
Yeltsin is currently following events from his hospital bed where he is preparing for heart surgery. Yastrzhembsky said he was working two to three hours a day.
